title: Media folders
lead: The folders inside this app where it may read your library's files, such as /media inside its container. Files outside them, or reached through a link that leads out of them, are never read.
listDescription: Give each folder's path as the app sees it. Saving doesn't look at the files: on the Library page, use Scan folders to find the files no library reported and Inspect files to read them all, or wait for the next sync.
empty: No folder yet: the app reads no file until you add one.
saveFailed: Could not save the media folders.
loadFailed: Could not load the media folders.
refreshFailed: Refresh failed, showing the last loaded folders.

replace.title: Replacing copies
replace.description: Whether a release you download may replace a copy you already have, and in which library folders. Saved with the folders above.
replace.switchHint: Off by default. When on, the Download dialog offers Replace after verification for copies in the folders ticked below, and the Duplicates page offers Remove this copy for files in them, to you alone. Once the new file is verified, the old copy moves into its media folder's quarantine, as a removed copy does at once, and stays there until you restore it or delete it for good. Moving needs the media folders mounted read-write and the app running as their owner, set with PUID and PGID.
replace.foldersHint: The folders of your Jellyfin libraries, as the app sees them. None is ticked by default, and the ticks are kept while replacement is off. A tick counts only inside the media folders as saved: a folder under one you add above can be ticked once you save it.
replace.outsideTicked: Outside the Media folders: this tick has no effect until the folder is inside one.
replace.noLonger: No longer a library folder the app knows, so a tick here has no effect. Saved unticked, it leaves this list.
replace.noFolders: No library folders yet: sync a library first.
replace.unmapped_one: {{value}} library folder has no path in this app: add a path mapping to the Jellyfin integration.
replace.unmapped_other: {{value}} library folders have no path in this app: add path mappings to the Jellyfin integration.
replace.renameClear: A move into the quarantine can work here: the same mount as the quarantine, mounted read-write, and writable by the app.

renameProblem.OtherMount: Not on the same mount as its media folder's quarantine, so a move would fail: mount the media folder as one read-write mount.
renameProblem.ReadOnly: Mounted read-only, so a move would fail: mount the media folders read-write.
renameProblem.NotWritable: The app's user can't write here or in its media folder, so a move would fail: set PUID and PGID for the app to the user and group that own your media folders, and restart it.
renameProblem.NotWritableRoot: The app can't write to {{path}}, which belongs to root, so a move would fail here: the app never runs as root, so it can move copies only in folders that belong to the user it runs as (now user {{appUserId}}, group {{appGroupId}}).
renameProblem.NotWritableAlreadyOwner: The app already runs as the owner of {{path}}, user {{appUserId}}, but the folder's permissions don't let its owner write there, so a move would fail: give the owner write permission on it.
renameProblem.NotWritableOtherOwner: The app runs as user {{appUserId}}, group {{appGroupId}}, and can't write to {{path}}, which belongs to user {{ownerUserId}}, group {{ownerGroupId}}, so a move would fail: set PUID={{ownerUserId}} and PGID={{ownerGroupId}} for the app in docker-compose.yml or .env, and restart it.
renameProblem.CouldNotCheck: The app couldn't check whether a move can work here; the move itself will tell.

replace.quarantineHint: Old copies wait in their media folder's quarantine until you restore them or delete them for good: a replaced copy on its job's page, under <jobs>Jobs</jobs>, a removed one under <removed>Removed copies</removed> on the Duplicates page.
